title: Halin's conjecture on hypomorphic infinite graphs
statement_text: If two infinite graphs are hypomorphic, then each is isomorphic to a subgraph of the other.
context_text: Two graphs $G$ and $H$ are hypomorphic if there is a bijection $\varphi\colon V(G)\to V(H)$ with $G - v \cong H - \varphi(v)$ for every vertex $v$. For finite graphs the Reconstruction Conjecture asserts that hypomorphic graphs are isomorphic; this fails for infinite graphs, and Halin's conjecture is the natural weakening.
notes: Bowler, Erde, Heinig, Lehner and Pitz, 'A counterexample to the reconstruction conjecture for locally finite trees' (Bull. London Math. Soc. 49, 2017), state that their construction also answers a question of Halin; the status review should check whether it is this one.

title: Barát–Thomassen conjecture
statement_text: For every tree $T$ there exists a natural number $k := k(T)$ such that every simple $k$-edge-connected graph whose number of edges is divisible by $e(T)$ admits a decomposition into copies of $T$.

related.note: Bensmail, Harutyunyan, Le and Thomassé propose a refinement of this conjecture

notes: Editorial lead, to be confirmed by the status review: Bensmail, Harutyunyan, Le, Merker and Thomassé, 'A proof of the Barát–Thomassen conjecture', J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 124 (2017).

title: Bondy's small cycle double cover conjecture
statement_text: Every simple graph on $n$ vertices without cut edges has a cycle double cover consisting of at most $n - 1$ cycles.
context_text: A cycle double cover is a family of cycles covering every edge exactly twice. This strengthens the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture (Appendix A, item 12).

title: Five cycle double cover conjecture
statement_text: Every 2-edge-connected graph has a double cover by at most five even subgraphs.
context_text: An even subgraph is a spanning subgraph in which every vertex has even degree, i.e. an edge-disjoint union of cycles; a double cover uses every edge exactly twice. Also attributed to Celmins (1984).

related.note: stronger form (prescribed cycle in the cover)
weaker: no bound on the number of even subgraphs

title: Linear arboricity conjecture
statement_text: Every simple $k$-regular graph has linear arboricity $\lceil (k+1)/2 \rceil$.
context_text: The linear arboricity $\mathrm{la}(G)$ is the least number of linear forests (forests whose components are paths) whose union is $G$. Equivalently: every simple graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ satisfies $\mathrm{la}(G) \le \lceil (\Delta+1)/2 \rceil$.
attributed_to: J. Akiyama, G. Exoo and F. Harary (1981); A.J.W. Hilton (1982)

title: Finding a second Hamilton cycle in a cubic graph
statement_text: Is the following problem in $\mathsf{P}$? Given a cubic graph $G$ and a Hamilton cycle in $G$, find a second Hamilton cycle in $G$.
context_text: By Smith's theorem every edge of a cubic graph lies in an even number of Hamilton cycles, so a second Hamilton cycle always exists; the question is whether one can be found in polynomial time.

related.note: existence of a second Hamilton cycle in regular graphs

title: Internally disjoint odd paths: is it in co-NP?
statement_text: Is the following problem in $\mathsf{co\text{-}NP}$? Given a graph $G$ and two $k$-subsets $X$ and $Y$ of $V(G)$, decide whether there exist $k$ internally disjoint $(X,Y)$-paths of odd length in $G$.

title: Thomassen's spanning k-connected bipartite subgraph conjecture
statement_text: Every $2k$-connected graph contains a spanning $k$-connected bipartite subgraph.
context_text: Thomassen (1989) asked more generally whether there is a function $f$ such that every $f(k)$-connected graph has a spanning $k$-connected bipartite subgraph; the book states the conjecture with $f(k) = 2k$.
notes: Translation caveat: the French edition prints « Tout graphe orienté 2k-connexe contient un sous-graphe orienté simple k-connexe couvrant » (digraph / oriented subgraph). Thomassen's 1989 question, as cited in the literature (Delcourt–Ferber 2015), concerns spanning bipartite subgraphs of undirected graphs; the statement above follows that reading. The status review should confirm against the English edition.

title: Orientable five cycle double cover conjecture
statement_text: Every 2-edge-connected graph has an orientable double cover by five even subgraphs.
context_text: A double cover by even subgraphs is orientable if each even subgraph can be oriented so that every edge of the graph is traversed once in each direction. Strengthens both the five cycle double cover conjecture (item 14) and the orientable cycle double cover conjecture.

related.note: its discussion lists this as a consequence of the strong form
compared with the orientable cycle double cover conjecture

title: Kelmans–Seymour conjecture
statement_text: Every 5-connected non-planar graph contains a subdivision of $K_5$.

title: Conway's thrackle conjecture
statement_text: No graph with more edges than vertices has a thrackle drawing.
context_text: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. French: « plongement en manoque ».

statement_text: If $G$ is a simple graph on $n$ vertices with $m > n(k-1)/2$ edges, then $G$ contains every tree with $k$ edges.

title: Even-cycle Turán number
statement_text: For every $k \ge 2$ there is a positive constant $c$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n, C_{2k}) \ge c\, n^{1+1/k}$.
context_text: $\mathrm{ex}(n, C_{2k})$ is the maximum number of edges of a simple graph on $n$ vertices with no cycle of length $2k$; the Bondy–Simonovits theorem gives the matching upper bound $O(n^{1+1/k})$. Known for $k = 2, 3, 5$.

title: Constructive exponential lower bound for diagonal Ramsey numbers
statement_text: Give a constructive proof that $r(k,k) \ge c^k$ for some constant $c > 1$ and all $k \ge 1$.
context_text: Erdős's 1947 probabilistic argument gives $r(k,k) \ge 2^{k/2}$ non-constructively.

title: Hadwiger's conjecture
statement_text: Every $k$-chromatic graph has a $K_k$-minor.
context_text: Known for $k \le 6$: the case $k = 5$ is equivalent to the Four Colour Theorem (Wagner 1937) and $k = 6$ was settled by Robertson, Seymour and Thomas (1993).
notes: Open Problem Garden itself has no page for this conjecture; only the list and fractional variants.

title: Hajós conjecture for $k = 5$ and $k = 6$
statement_text: Does every $k$-chromatic graph contain a subdivision of $K_k$ when $k = 5$ and when $k = 6$?
context_text: Hajós conjectured this for all $k$; it holds for $k \le 4$ (Dirac 1952) and Catlin (1979) disproved it for every $k \ge 7$.

title: Erdős–Lovász Tihany conjecture
statement_text: Let $G$ be a $k$-chromatic graph containing no $k$-clique, and let $k + 1 = k_1 + k_2$ with $k_1, k_2 \ge 2$. Then $G$ has vertex-disjoint subgraphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ such that $G_i$ is $k_i$-chromatic, $i = 1, 2$.

title: Gyárfás's tree conjecture for triangle-free graphs
statement_text: Every triangle-free graph of infinite chromatic number contains every finite tree as an induced subgraph.
context_text: Follows from the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture (Appendix A, item 49): if $T$-free graphs are $\chi$-bounded, a triangle-free $T$-free graph has bounded chromatic number.

statement_text: Every toroidal graph has three vertices whose deletion leaves a 4-colourable graph.

title: Chromatic number of the plane (Hadwiger–Nelson problem)
statement_text: Determine the chromatic number of the unit-distance graph of the plane, i.e. the least number of colours needed to colour the points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ so that no two points at distance $1$ receive the same colour.
context_text: At the time of the book, $4 \le \chi(\mathbb{R}^2) \le 7$.
notes: Editorial lead, to be confirmed by the status review: de Grey (2018) showed the chromatic number is at least 5.

title: 1-factorization conjecture
statement_text: Every simple $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices with $n$ even and $d \ge n/2$ is $d$-edge-colourable.
context_text: Equivalently, such graphs have a 1-factorization. Usually stated (Chetwynd and Hilton 1985) with the sharper threshold $d \ge 2\lceil n/4 \rceil - 1$.
notes: Editorial lead, to be confirmed by the status review: Csaba, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Treglown, 'Proof of the 1-factorization and Hamilton decomposition conjectures', Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 244 (2016), for sufficiently large $n$.

title: Vizing's interchange conjecture
statement_text: Given a proper edge colouring of a graph $G$, a proper edge colouring of $G$ with $\chi'(G)$ colours can be obtained by a sequence of colour interchanges on alternating paths or cycles (Kempe changes).
notes: Editorial lead, to be confirmed by the status review: Narboni, 'Vizing's edge-recoloring conjecture holds' (arXiv:2302.12914, 2023); triangle-free case by Bonamy, Defrain, Klimošová, Lagoutte and Narboni (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2023).

title: Kotzig's unique $k$-path conjecture
statement_text: For $k \ge 3$ there is no graph in which every pair of vertices is connected by a unique path of length $k$.
context_text: The case $k = 2$ is the Friendship Theorem (Theorem 3.1 in the book).

title: Smith's conjecture on longest cycles
statement_text: In a $k$-connected graph, $k \ge 2$, any two longest cycles have at least $k$ vertices in common.
context_text: Attributed to S. Smith; see Grötschel (1984).

title: Birmelé's conjecture on long cycles
statement_text: If any two cycles of length at least $k$ in a graph intersect, then the graph has a set of $k$ vertices meeting every cycle of length at least $k$.

title: Weighted Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture
statement_text: Let $D$ be a strongly connected digraph with a positive weight function $w$ on its arcs such that $w^-(v) \ge 1$ and $w^+(v) \ge 1$ for every vertex $v$. Then $D$ contains a directed cycle of weight at least $1$.
context_text: $w^-(v)$ and $w^+(v)$ denote the total weight of the arcs entering and leaving $v$. Bollobás and Scott proved the analogous statement for directed paths.

related.note: the unweighted case; this statement appears in its discussion

title: Matthews–Sumner conjecture
statement_text: Every 4-connected claw-free graph is Hamiltonian.
context_text: Equivalent, via Ryjáček's closure, to Thomassen's conjecture that every 4-connected line graph is Hamiltonian.

statement_text: All but finitely many connected vertex-transitive graphs are Hamiltonian.
context_text: Only five connected vertex-transitive graphs without a Hamilton cycle are known: $K_2$, the Petersen graph, the Coxeter graph, and the truncations of the last two.
